Repeat the same action repeatedly while expecting a different outcome — that is the definition of insanity.

This quote also appears to neatly encapsulate the message Republicans are sending voters ahead of the midterms.

And we mean that sincerely.

Political analysts say the data currently points to a potential "blue wave" returning the House to Democratic control, driven in part by Donald Trump's sagging approval numbers.

Republicans are heading toward a drubbing in House races unless the party can articulate a compelling case for continued governance.

House Speaker Mike Johnson had a chance to make that case to voters during an appearance on CNBC's "Squawk Box" on Tuesday — and he did a remarkable favor: for Democrats.

"For the next two years, we're going to be doing exactly what we've been doing, which is setting the conditions for a strong America," Johnson said.

He went on to elaborate:

Johnson attempted to win over voters by promising a continuation of the very policies that have led to conflict with Iran, higher gas prices, and inflation — a pitch that, unsurprisingly, failed to land.

In fact, it landed just about as well as Vice President JD Vance's shameless plea earlier this month for voters to "give us another chance."
